content.text:
`out/module.ts` is written, and it type-checks. The only `tsc` errors are in the original `src/module.ts`, where the `lodash` imports can't be resolved because lodash isn't installed.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 741 bytes (min+gzip) and 113 bytes of own code. I did not run the size command on the original, so I have no baseline for the own-code allowance.

I also did not run a result comparison against the original. The only behaviour check was one `truncate` call on a 50-character string, which gave 21 `a`s plus `...`, the expected 24-character result.

What changed, by function:

| Function | Before | After | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pick` | `lodash/pick` | `es-toolkit` `pick(row, ['id','name'])` | Same call shape. |
| `sumBy` | `lodash/sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `es-toolkit` `sumBy(rows, r => r.age)` | The strict version takes only a function, so the `'age'` shorthand became a one-line arrow function. |
| `truncate` | `lodash/truncate` | `es-toolkit/compat` `truncate(text, { length: 24 })` | There is no strict `truncate` in the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2, so the compat version is the only one that keeps the behaviour. |

No lodash import remains, and nothing was installed. The exported `Row` and `Config` types and the three function signatures are unchanged. The migrated code is:

```ts
import { pick, sumBy } from 'es-toolkit';
import { truncate } from 'es-toolkit/compat';
```
